question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay for config, tool, and system defaults, or keep immutable baseline checks in conformance-only Policy/Nix-style surfaces?
rationale: This changes the security boundary, config precedence, runtime write behavior, diagnostics, and upgrade expectations; current main only supplies adjacent conformance checks and Nix-managed config immutability.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only surfaces
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for audits while runtime config remains the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer for hook design
options.body: Keep this issue open until related policy-hook proposals decide whether enforcement belongs in plugin hooks or core config/write paths.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns this issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest decision owner for the security boundary.
